correctness.rationale: From L16=2207 and F16=987 the principal logarithm has exact valuation one. The fourteen branches with F_r nonzero modulo seven have normalized derivatives (5/2)F_r units, hence are isometries onto five complete residue balls. On the remaining two branches a convergent hyperbolic-sine normalized function H is a 7-adic isometric bijection, giving exactly 2+2205 H(t)^2 and -2-2205 H(t+1/2)^2. Square-root counts and a regular branch certify all per-residue frequencies and the exact least period. Verified independently by recurrence enumeration at exponents 1..5; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2025 density agreement is not an implication of this Lucas frequency classification. Its sequence is Fibonacci (initial values 0,1), not Lucas (2,1), and the 2025 theorem gives limiting density rather than all individual frequencies; the 7-adic images occupy different residue classes and critical indices. Abstract-level 2024 comparison remains a residual risk, not a claimed whole-document exclusion. The broad earlier recurrence-bounds framework is not ignored: the inspected 2007 main theorem is inapplicable at e=1, and the 1999 chapter is a residual uncertain stronger-coverage risk. The accessible descriptions claim bounds rather than the exact all-exponent prime-7 Lucas frequencies.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The asserted formulas for all 7-power residue frequencies and exact 7-adic Lucas image imply the known failure of completeness at 49, but the reverse implication does not hold. Earlier prime-2/3/5 formulas are different prime-local cases. The 2025 Fibonacci theorem covers a different initial condition and only density, so it cannot imply a specific Lucas individual-residue multiplicity function without a further theorem, which the inspected work does not provide. General upper/lower frequency bounds do not imply the complete exact per-residue function unless they coincide in this case; the available statements do not show such sharp coincidence, and the primary 1999 material remains a risk.

originality.rationale: Primary comparisons separate exact Lucas frequencies for p=2,3,5 from mere Lucas residue completeness for p=7, and from the Fibonacci-only 2025 limiting-density result. The new theorem provides all per-residue Lucas frequencies at p=7 and an exact pair of quadratic images; unindexed general recurrence results remain a real priority risk. Carlip–Somer general frequency bounds were examined through their 2007 primary article; Theorem 6.1 there assumes e>1, whereas e=nu_7(F8)=1. Their 1999 regular recurrence chapter was unavailable in full and remains a distinct risk.
residual_risks: The 2024 generic Lucas recurrence paper was available only at abstract level; its full proof was not inspected.
The short Avila–Chen paper was available only as publisher abstract, although the separate Lang–Lang proof was fully accessible.
A different-index or general-second-order recurrence theorem could contain the same frequency formula without matching keywords; no unique historical-priority claim is made.

value.rationale: After the known completeness modulo seven fails at the next prime-power level, the exact spectrum and each residue frequency are nontrivial natural invariants. Two explicit quadratic local images explain exception classes and high multiplicity, with 14 regular branches explaining baseline multiplicities. Coinciding with a known Fibonacci limiting density is not alone the value; the entire Lucas all-exponent distribution is.
